concerns.concern: The fit holds a single relaxation time τ fixed across all aging times. Any change in decay rate with aging is therefore forced into the exponent β, so the claimed β = 1 → 1.5 'jamming transition' may be a fitting artifact.
concerns.quote: A single τ is forced across all aging times, so any change in decay rate is pushed into β.

concerns.concern: The fitted τ values are 10–50× longer than the sampled delay range, and g2 decays by only a fraction of a percent. τ and β are strongly degenerate in this regime, yet no free-τ fits and no β uncertainties or covariances are shown.
concerns.quote: Relaxation times of 35,000–160,000 s are extracted from windows of only a few thousand seconds, with g2 decaying by a fraction of a percent.

concerns.concern: The Arrhenius activation energy depends largely on the 298 K point, which the authors describe as the experimental stability limit. That point may reflect instrumental limits rather than thermally activated dynamics.
concerns.quote: If it is the instrumental stability limit, it does not reflect intrinsic thermally activated dynamics and should not anchor an Arrhenius fit.

concerns.concern: Deterministic filament formation and 'learning' are inferred only from correlations between consecutive cycles. A rise in that quantity could equally come from slower overall evolution, thermal settling, cumulative heating or beam/current-induced changes. There is no fixed reference-cycle or G(n, n+k) analysis.
concerns.quote: ΔG(n, n+1) compares only consecutive cycles. A rise in this quantity is also expected if the overall configuration simply evolves more slowly with time.

concerns.concern: The claim that a sub-threshold current resets the learned state and restores stochastic switching is never tested. There is no train, erase, re-cycle experiment.
concerns.quote: The 'reset' half of the train/reset claim is therefore an extrapolation.

concerns.concern: No electrical switching statistics, such as threshold voltage spread versus cycle number, are given to show that switching stochasticity actually decreases.
concerns.quote: no such electrical stochasticity data are presented.

concerns.concern: The 4 mA relaxation time is slower than even the no-current room-temperature value, which is the opposite of what Joule heating would produce. The 'larger phase-space' argument offered instead is speculative.
concerns.quote: The 4 mA relaxation time is slower than even the no-current room-temperature value, which is hard to reconcile with Joule-heating-driven dynamics.

concerns.concern: The current dependence of the jamming time is not statistically supported. The 0.26 and 1.7 mA values are indistinguishable, and the 4 mA data never reach β = 1.5, contradicting 'for all currents'. The shear-thickening analogy is therefore unjustified.
concerns.quote: A monotonic current dependence, and the analogy to shear thickening, cannot be inferred from these numbers.

concerns.concern: The 298 K decay time in the text (8000 s) disagrees by an order of magnitude with the value in Fig. 2c (81,000 s).
concerns.quote: These differ by an order of magnitude, so one is presumably a typo, but it matters.

concerns.concern: The beam footprint is larger than the 5×5 µm channel, so VO2 outside the current path contributes speckle. This dilutes or biases the correlations, and current-induced sample drift is not addressed.
concerns.quote: That material contributes to the speckle without participating in filament formation.

concerns.concern: The paper does not state which detector ROI, q-range or Bragg reflection (M1, R or both) the correlations use, nor whether a single rocking angle was used or peak drift was corrected. Decorrelation therefore cannot be attributed to domain rearrangement rather than strain or peak motion.
concerns.quote: It is not stated whether correlations are computed over the M1 peak, the R peak, or both together, or what pixel ROI and q-range are used.

concerns.concern: The normalization in Eqs. (1)–(2) by ⟨I²⟩ is inconsistent with the g2 = 1 + A|F|² baseline and with the plotted values above 1. The averaging in the numerator is also unspecified.
concerns.quote: The definitions are internally inconsistent with g2 = 1 + A|F|²

concerns.concern: The claimed coincidence of the 'learning' timescale with the jamming time is unsupported, because jamming was measured under DC current rather than under cycling.
concerns.quote: the coincidence of the 'learning' timescale with t_jam is asserted, but jamming was measured under DC current, not cycling.

concerns.concern: The normalization used to scale the cycle-to-cycle correlation ΔG to [0,1] is not specified.
concerns.quote: The normalization used to scale ΔG to [0,1] is also unspecified.

concerns.concern: β = 1.5 is a compressed exponential, typically linked to ballistic, stress-driven relaxation. Interpreting it as glassy or jammed dynamics is only one possible reading, not a direct signature.
concerns.quote: Interpreting β = 1.5 as jamming is therefore one possible reading, not a direct signature of it.

concerns.concern: The 1.7 mA measurement appears only in Fig. 4 and is never described: no two-time map, protocol, or statement of whether it is above threshold.
concerns.quote: The 1.7 mA measurement appears only in Fig. 4. It is never described

concerns.concern: The number of temperatures used in the Arrhenius fit (Fig. 2d inset) is not stated.
concerns.quote: The number of temperatures in the inset of Fig. 2d is also not stated.

concerns.concern: Comparing the activation energy to the VO2 melting temperature is physically loose. A numerical coincidence does not link a microscopic domain-motion barrier to melting, and the argument conflates domain mobility with liquefaction.
concerns.quote: A numerical coincidence between Ea/k_B and T_m does not show that the mechanisms are related.

concerns.concern: The beam is several times larger than the coherence length, giving very low (~2%) contrast and poor signal-to-noise for the sub-percent decays being fitted.
concerns.quote: The beam is also ~4–9× larger than the 1.7 µm coherence length, consistent with the very low (~2%) contrast.

concerns.concern: The cycling timing is ambiguous. On/Off durations, duty cycle and detector window placement are unclear, and the stated time-to-cycle correspondence (200 cycles at 1000 s) does not match the ~3 s per cycle axis.
concerns.quote: With 3 s per cycle, 200 cycles is ~600 s, not 1000 s

concerns.concern: Several numbers disagree between text and figures: the sub-threshold current is 0.26 vs 0.27 mA, and the 4 mA τ is 150,000 vs 160,000 s.
concerns.quote: Several numbers and descriptions conflict: 0.26 vs 0.27 mA, 150,000 vs 160,000 s

concerns.concern: The 0.26 mA data are described as 'after electrical switching', although this current is sub-threshold and no switching occurs.
concerns.quote: calling the 0.26 mA data 'after electrical switching' is inconsistent with it being sub-threshold, with no switching.

concerns.concern: The Methods say the devices were globally irradiated, whereas the main text says only a central 5×5 µm region of one device was irradiated and the other device is pristine.
concerns.quote: devices were globally irradiated using a 30 keV focused Ga+ ion beam

concerns.concern: The domain size derived from the Bragg peak width is a structural coherence length limited by thickness, grains or strain, not the metallic/insulating domain size. The reflection, direction and temperature used are also unspecified.
concerns.quote: this is affected by thickness, grain size and strain broadening, so it is not specifically the size of metallic versus insulating domains.

concerns.concern: Describing the device as 'fully switched' contradicts the filamentary picture, in which most of the channel stays insulating.
concerns.quote: Calling the region 'fully switched' contradicts that picture.

concerns.concern: Eq. (2) reuses τ as the dummy time variable, which clashes with τ as the relaxation time in Eq. (3).
concerns.quote: Eq. (2) further reuses τ as the dummy time variable, which clashes with τ as the relaxation time in Eq. (3).

concerns.concern: Eq. (3) is called a 'single exponential decay function' even though it includes the exponent β, i.e. it is a stretched/compressed exponential.
concerns.quote: The Methods also call Eq. (3) 'a single exponential decay function', although it includes β.

concerns.concern: The text refers to an 'inset (orange data)', but Fig. 3i is a separate panel.
concerns.quote: The text also refers to an 'inset (orange data)', but Fig. 3i is a separate panel.
